title: Переломы и вывихи
terminology: Fracture or luxation is a whole-patient trauma problem before it is an image of one limb.
Weight bearing does not exclude a clinically important fracture.
Open fracture requires wound-to-fracture communication assessment; wound size alone cannot classify it.
Pain, distal perfusion, motor and sensation are recorded before and after temporary support.
Orthogonal radiographs include adjacent joints when safe; CT or specialist planning is selected for complex anatomy.
Temporary support is location- and configuration-dependent and never proves union.
Articular and physeal injuries preserve congruity, growth and longitudinal alignment risks.
Pelvic and axial trauma preserves urinary, rectal, airway, nutrition and neurologic priorities.
Patellar luxation is classified by function, pain, progression and anatomy; an incidental finding does not mandate surgery.
Pathologic fracture is investigated before definitive fixation choice and biopsy route preserves future treatment planes.
No drug, dose, implant, reduction manoeuvre, splint construction or operative technique is generated by this package.

commonHistoryQuestions.prompt: Что произошло, когда и какой была энергия события?
Мог ли пациент идти после события и сколько шагов?
Есть ли рядом рана, кровь, выделения или exposed material?
Менялись ли цвет, температура или отёк дистальной конечности?
Наблюдалось ли движение пальцев или необычная потеря чувствительности?
Были ли раньше хромота, припухлость, операция или имплант?
Есть ли мочеиспускание и дефекация после тазовой травмы?
Что и когда давали дома от боли?
Кем и когда наложена повязка/шина и как выглядят пальцы?
Может ли семья обеспечить ограничение активности и уход?
Есть ли датированные снимки, операции и данные имплантов?
Каков доступный сейчас бюджет и возможен ли поэтапный план?

variants.title: Закрытый относительно стабильный перелом конечности
variants.diagnosticTruth: Closed, relatively stable configuration with documented whole-patient stability, soft tissues and distal neurovascular status; support eligibility is anatomy-specific.

presentations.complaint: Young patient with painful limb after trauma and incomplete or minimally displaced closed fracture.

investigations.result: Stable patient and concurrent injury record.
Incomplete/minimally displaced configuration and physis context.

followUp.timing: early alignment then authored union/growth checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Stable fracture remains aligned with age-specific monitoring.
outcomes.unsafe: Young age is treated as proof of harmless healing.

ownerCommunication: Explain why early recheck is required even if the patient starts using the limb.

presentations.complaint: Distal paw fracture involving selected digits or metacarpal/metatarsal bones.

examFindings.finding: Generic paw bandage is not definitive.

investigations.result: Bones, digits, displacement and joint involvement.
Position, toes, skin and perfusion record.

followUp.timing: early support check and serial healing assessment

outcomes.safe: Support is selected only for an eligible distal pattern.
outcomes.unsafe: Every paw fracture receives the same bandage.

ownerCommunication: Show which toe, skin and slippage changes require urgent return.

presentations.complaint: Eligible fracture is comfortable and aligned after temporary support, pending healing or definitive plan.

historyAnswers.existing_splint_bandage_status: Who applied it, date, slippage/odor/swelling authored.
historyAnswers.post_event_weight_bearing: Restricted; not used as union proof.

examFindings.finding: Perfusion and pressure injury override schedule.

investigations.result: Support position, skin, toes and perfusion.

followUp.timing: scheduled support and union checkpoints plus urgent red flags

outcomes.safe: Comfort and alignment progress without premature activity.
outcomes.unsafe: Support is mistaken for completed healing.

ownerCommunication: Explain that reduced pain is welcome but does not authorize unrestricted activity.

variants.title: Нестабильный, смещённый или оскольчатый перелом
variants.diagnosticTruth: Unstable fracture requires whole-patient stabilization, documented soft-tissue and neurovascular state, location-appropriate temporary protection and specialist repair planning.

presentations.complaint: Painful non-weight-bearing limb with abnormal alignment from displaced long-bone fracture.

investigations.result: Pain, motor, sensation and distal perfusion.
Displacement, segment and associated joint injury.

followUp.timing: urgent receiving-service and post-support neurovascular checkpoint

outcomes.safe: Patient and limb reach repair planning without added injury.
outcomes.unsafe: The UI offers reduction before imaging or a universal splint.

ownerCommunication: Explain why temporary protection is not the same as definitive repair.

presentations.complaint: High-energy comminuted fracture with substantial soft-tissue and concurrent-trauma risk.

historyAnswers.post_event_weight_bearing: Usually absent; not sole severity marker.

examFindings.finding: Energy, perfusion and soft tissue remain explicit.

followUp.timing: continuous stabilization then staged soft-tissue and repair checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Repair category reflects biology and whole-patient status.
outcomes.unsafe: A simple label or price hides soft-tissue severity.

ownerCommunication: Give staged estimates and uncertainty without guaranteeing limb salvage.

presentations.complaint: Multiple limbs or multiple levels are fractured, creating mobility, nursing and sequencing risk.

historyAnswers.post_event_weight_bearing: Unable or unsafe to assess walking.

examFindings.finding: All injuries and pressure risks planned.
Cheapest single-limb repair cannot discard other sites.

followUp.timing: same-episode injury map and staged mobility/function checkpoints

outcomes.safe: All injuries remain visible through sequencing and recovery.
outcomes.unsafe: One repaired limb closes a multi-injury episode.

ownerCommunication: Explain sequencing, hospitalization and why no injury is silently dropped.

variants.title: Открытый перелом или тяжёлое повреждение мягких тканей
variants.diagnosticTruth: Any communicating wound creates an open-fracture route; contamination, perfusion and tissue viability determine urgency and staged reconstruction uncertainty.

presentations.complaint: Puncture-sized wound near a fracture may communicate with bone despite limited skin damage.

followUp.timing: urgent surgical handoff and infection/union checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Small communicating wound receives open-fracture care.
outcomes.unsafe: Small size leads to cosmetic closure and missed contamination.

ownerCommunication: Explain why a tiny skin wound can still be a serious open fracture.

presentations.complaint: Crush or high-energy open fracture with contamination and uncertain tissue viability.

followUp.timing: continuous viability then staged reconstruction/infection checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Staged specialist plan reflects tissue evolution.
outcomes.unsafe: The game guarantees salvage from the first image.

ownerCommunication: Give uncertainty and staged estimates without promising limb preservation.

presentations.complaint: Delayed open fracture with discharge, odor, exposed material or increasing pain and infection risk.

examFindings.finding: Not converted into an unrelated abscess.
Surface swab alone is not decision-quality evidence.

followUp.timing: urgent source-control plan and serial infection/union review

outcomes.safe: Delayed infection risk remains connected to fracture care.
outcomes.unsafe: It becomes a superficial abscess or empiric endless treatment.

ownerCommunication: Explain why delay changes tissue and infection uncertainty without assigning blame.

variants.title: Внутрисуставной перелом или повреждение зоны роста
variants.diagnosticTruth: Articular congruity and open growth plate status change planning and make arthritis, length and alignment longitudinal authored outcomes.

presentations.complaint: Fracture disrupts an articular surface and threatens joint congruity and cartilage function.

investigations.result: Union, joint function and arthritis trajectory.

followUp.timing: specialist planning then union and joint-function checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Joint anatomy and long-term function drive decisions.
outcomes.unsafe: A small fragment is dismissed after pain improves.

ownerCommunication: Explain why joint-surface injury can matter beyond bone union.

presentations.complaint: Juvenile fracture crosses an open growth plate with future length and alignment risk.

examFindings.finding: Length and alignment compared through growth.

followUp.timing: early alignment, union and through-growth checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Growth disturbance is detected early and remains attributable.
outcomes.unsafe: Union closes the case before growth is assessed.

ownerCommunication: Explain why a healed fracture can still affect later limb growth.

presentations.complaint: Cat has acute or chronic hip lameness compatible with capital physeal fracture or slipped epiphysis, sometimes without remembered trauma.

historyAnswers.post_event_weight_bearing: Acute non-weight-bearing or chronic reduced jumping.

investigations.result: Capital physis, displacement and opposite hip.

followUp.timing: specialist decision and bilateral function/growth checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Atraumatic and bilateral risk are evaluated without breed shortcut.
outcomes.unsafe: No trauma or breed label decides the diagnosis.

ownerCommunication: Explain that this growth-plate injury can occur without a witnessed accident.

variants.title: Перелом таза или осевой скелет с сопутствующей травмой
variants.diagnosticTruth: Pelvic and axial fractures preserve concurrent thoracic, abdominal, urinary, rectal, airway, nutrition and neurologic priorities before bone-only repair decisions.

presentations.complaint: Pelvic fracture with variable ability to stand or walk and possible acetabular/weight-bearing involvement.

historyAnswers.post_event_weight_bearing: Steps possible or absent; not exclusion.

examFindings.finding: Conservative versus surgery category is specialist-reviewed.

followUp.timing: same-episode organ screen then mobility/elimination/function checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Pelvis is managed with organ and weight-bearing context.
outcomes.unsafe: Walking permits bone-only discharge.

ownerCommunication: Explain that a few steps do not rule out pelvic or internal injury.

presentations.complaint: Pelvic trauma includes inability to urinate, hematuria, rectal concern, tail/perineal deficit or canal narrowing.

followUp.timing: continuous elimination/neuro monitoring and receiving-service checkpoint

outcomes.safe: Organ and neurologic risks are resolved or safely transferred.
outcomes.unsafe: Bone alignment closes the case while elimination is unknown.

ownerCommunication: Explain why urination, defecation and nerve function determine safe discharge.

presentations.complaint: Mandibular, spinal or other axial fracture creates airway, occlusion, nutrition, immobilization or neurologic priorities.

followUp.timing: continuous airway/neuro/nutrition monitoring and specialist outcome

outcomes.safe: Site-specific priorities reach specialist care without invented technique.
outcomes.unsafe: Generic limb logic is applied to jaw or spine.

ownerCommunication: Explain the site-specific danger and why specialist stabilization is required.

variants.title: Травматический вывих или клинически значимый подвывих
variants.diagnosticTruth: Joint luxation requires whole-patient and associated-fracture assessment, imaging-defined congruence and reviewed reduction/surgery eligibility with post-reduction verification and longitudinal function.

presentations.complaint: Acute painful hip luxation after trauma with altered limb carriage and associated-injury risk.

examFindings.finding: Urinary, thoracic and other injury remain visible.

investigations.result: Concurrent trauma and anesthetic risk context.
Direction, associated fracture and post-route congruence.

followUp.timing: urgent specialist route then congruence/reluxation/function checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Reduction eligibility and post-route stability are documented.
outcomes.unsafe: The joint is blindly put back and the episode closes.

ownerCommunication: Explain why imaging is needed before and after a reduction route.

presentations.complaint: Elbow, shoulder, carpus, tarsus or another joint is luxated/subluxated with possible ligament, fracture or neurovascular injury.

investigations.result: Pain, distal perfusion, motor and sensation.

followUp.timing: pre/post-route congruence and longitudinal joint-function review

outcomes.safe: Associated injuries and rehabilitation remain visible.
outcomes.unsafe: Reduction erases fracture, ligament or nerve risk.

ownerCommunication: Explain that restoring position does not by itself restore stability or function.

presentations.complaint: Patellar luxation is incidental/asymptomatic or causes skipping, pain, deformity or progressive dysfunction.

examFindings.finding: Function, pain, progression and anatomy decide route.
One knee cannot hide the other.

investigations.result: Side, direction, stability, pain and function.

followUp.timing: same-scale bilateral function and progression checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Incidental cases can be monitored and symptomatic cases planned proportionately.
outcomes.unsafe: Every luxating patella earns surgery or every incidental finding is ignored.

ownerCommunication: Explain the difference between an anatomic finding and clinically important dysfunction.

variants.title: Патологический перелом, нарушение сращения или осложнение ремонта
variants.diagnosticTruth: Low-energy fracture, failed healing, implant/bandage/reduction complication remains linked to original anatomy and episode while biology, mechanics, infection and neoplasia are investigated without blame.

presentations.complaint: Low-energy fracture or fracture through a site with prior pain, swelling or abnormal bone.

examFindings.finding: Metabolic, infectious and neoplastic causes remain.

investigations.result: Systemic, infectious, metabolic or neoplastic route.

followUp.timing: urgent staging/biopsy plan then cause-specific fracture outcome

outcomes.safe: Cause and biopsy route shape definitive repair.
outcomes.unsafe: The fracture is fixed before cause/staging or sampled through future planes.

ownerCommunication: Explain why a weak-bone fracture needs cause testing before final repair choice.

presentations.complaint: Fracture shows slow, absent or misaligned healing on serial clinical and imaging review.

historyAnswers.prior_images_and_implant_records: Serial dated images and repair record fixed.
historyAnswers.confinement_feasibility: Actual restriction and barriers recorded without blame.

examFindings.finding: One image or calendar date is insufficient.
More time is not the only answer.

investigations.result: Alignment, union, implant and function trajectory.

followUp.timing: serial same-scale biology/mechanics/function checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Failure mode is identified before revision or continued monitoring.
outcomes.unsafe: The owner is blamed or only more time is offered.

ownerCommunication: Explain whether the concern is biology, stability, infection, alignment or several factors.

presentations.complaint: Broken/migrated implant, pressure injury, loss of reduction or reluxation after prior fracture/joint care.

historyAnswers.prior_images_and_implant_records: Original procedure and implant/reduction record fixed.

examFindings.finding: Calendar schedule cannot override red flags.

investigations.result: Implant, alignment, union and reduction status.

followUp.timing: urgent red-flag resolution then revision/reluxation outcome

outcomes.safe: Complication is triaged and attributed without losing prior evidence.
outcomes.unsafe: A new episode hides prior treatment outcome or urgent pressure injury.

ownerCommunication: Explain the complication, immediate risk and revision/salvage uncertainty without blame.

familyValidationRules: Reject if life-threatening trauma is delayed for limb imaging.
Reject if open status is inferred from wound size alone.
Reject if distal neurovascular status is missing before or after support.
Reject if every fracture receives the same splint or any unsuitable proximal support lacks referral.
Reject if code generates a drug, dose, implant, reduction manoeuvre or operative technique.
Reject if external imaging, surgery or longitudinal healing returns instantly.
